messages:
Ajay: Heads-up — I'm proposing a small but widespread change to audit events we send to customers and to S3 exports: add actor_ip and remove session_id. Need alignment on versioning + backfill strategy and KMS impact.

Keiko: quick q — why remove session_id? some consumers use it to stitch sessions for analytics.

Ajay: session_id is noisy and often null for API key flows. We prefer actor_ip for forensics. We can keep session_id in internal logs but drop from customer-facing stream.

Sofia: +1 for actor_ip, but we need a plan for customers that expect session_id field — they will break. can we emit schema_version in every event and provide a compat window?

Ben: Suggest schema_version and a header x-audit-schema: v2 in the export manifest. Backfill: backfill v2 for last 90 days? that's heavy.

Marta: Backfill cost concern noted. We can produce a compatibility shim that injects session_id=null for v1 consumers for a while instead of full backfill. cheaper and safer.

Ajay: Draft proposal idea: 1) Introduce schema_version in events (string) 2) Start emitting v2 (actor_ip present, session_id omitted) behind feature-flag for hosted API + dedicated customers with opt-in. 3) For exports, include metadata file manifest.json listing schema_version and a compatibility shim option.

Keiko: How does KMS play here? Are we changing any fields that are encrypted or signed today?

Ben: We currently HMAC the audit payload with KMS-derived key and store ciphertext for exports. Adding a field means HMAC diff for consumers that validate integrity. We'll need to coordinate key rotation and change consumer validation docs.

Sofia: For HMAC consumers we should provide a transitional validation mode: publish the new signing key and a validation mode that accepts both v1 and v2 payloads for 14 days. That reduces breakage.

Marta: operational checklist I propose: 
1) feature-flag v2 emit for internal only 
2) update KMS signing docs + publish new key id 
3) rollout opt-in to a small set of customers 
4) generate shimmed export manifest for historical data 
5) deprecate session_id in public docs with 30d notice

Ajay: +1. Also need RBAC note: removing session_id affects tenant-level read filters in some SSO flows. Product/Integrations to confirm no search filters rely on session_id. @Keiko can you sync with Integrations?

Keiko: Will do. FYI I pinged integrations and data-platform. They want a spec doc and a sample payload diff.

Ben: Here's a quick sample payload diff we can use in the spec: 
```json
// v1 (current)
{
  "schema_version": "v1",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-12T18:22:01Z",
  "actor": { "id": "user_123", "type": "user" },
  "session_id": "sess-9a8b7c",
  "action": "model.deploy"
}

// v2 (proposed)
{
  "schema_version": "v2",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-12T18:22:01Z",
  "actor": { "id": "user_123", "type": "user" },
  "actor_ip": "198.51.100.23",
  "action": "model.deploy"
}
```

Sofia: Nice. Add note that actor_ip will be redacted for PII-sensitive customers or when forwarding to downstreams. We'll need a flag per-tenant for ip_redaction.

Marta: Also call out retention: if we keep session_id internally for 90d, make sure exports respect customer retention settings.

Ajay: Good catches. Action items: 
- Keiko: spec + sample payloads (due EOD Fri)
- Ben: KMS/HMAC transition plan + keys doc (due Mon)
- Marta: export manifest format + shim plan (due Tue)
- Sofia: privacy controls for actor_ip + per-tenant redaction flag (due Mon)

deploy-bot: Reminder: engineering-design-review scheduled today 16:00 to review audit schema changes.

Keiko: I'll post the first draft spec in this thread when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
